title: EpiLing-Multicenterstudy for the evaluation of the EpiLing-Tool
summary:
It is possible to differentiate between epileptic and dissociative seizures based solely on the way in which the patients report these seizures. Until now, recognizing these differences was largely reserved for linguists. The Bielefeld EpiLing group has now developed a list of criteria, the so-called "EpiLing Tool", with criteria that doctors can also recognize during the initial encounter. 
The group was able to show that doctors who listen to recordings of conversations can use the EpiLing-Tool after a one-day training course and are highly likely to make the correct diagnosis. 
The EpiLing-Multicenterstudy intends to clarify the sensitivity and spezitivity with which the EpiLing-Tool distinguishes epileptic from dissociativ seizures when the doctors are not sitting relaxed and concentrated in a training session, but are using the tool as part of their normal clinical routine.

interventions.name:
We assume that every participating clinic that admits patients for a diagnostic workup of seizures conducts a doctor-patient encounter as part of the initial examinations.
